explanation: Property investments include residential, commercial, industrial and specialised assets, held for rent, development or resale. Each has different demand, lease terms, costs and financing. Location and asset quality matter, but investment returns also depend on entry price and capital requirements.
Owning land, developing a building and operating a leased property are distinct economic activities. Compare income, liquidity and execution risk rather than grouping every property as one asset.

types.name: Land investment
types.explanation: Depends largely on future use or resale.

workedCase.setup: A buyer compares a rented building earning ₹8 lakh NOI with vacant land at the same ₹100 price.
steps: The building has observable operating income.
The land requires assumptions about development or resale.
Compare future investment, timing and permissions.
workedCase.result: Equal purchase prices do not imply equal risk or income.
workedCase.interpretation: No universal appreciation rate is assumed.

analysis: Model costs, income and exit separately.

explanation: Property income starts with potential rent, then deducts vacancy, concessions and collection losses to reach effective income. Operating costs maintain the asset's service, while financing, depreciation and capital expenditure require separate treatment. Lease wording determines who bears costs.
Vacancy can raise costs as well as reduce income. Tenant quality, expiry concentration and rent-free periods affect cash timing.

types.name: Potential rent
types.explanation: Income at stated occupancy and pricing.

workedCase.setup: Potential annual rent is ₹12 lakh, vacancy loss ₹2 and operating costs ₹3.
steps: NOI is ₹7 before financing and capex.
workedCase.result: NOI falls to ₹6 if costs remain unchanged.
workedCase.interpretation: Maintenance classification and pass-through charges require consistent definitions.

explanation: Net operating income measures property income less defined operating expenses before financing and income tax. A capitalisation rate relates stabilised annual NOI to value. It is a pricing ratio, not a guaranteed total return or a discount rate interchangeable in every model.
Capitalising unstable income without adjustment can mislead. Growth, required capex, risk and market conditions affect the appropriate valuation.

types.name: NOI
types.explanation: Property operating income under a stated definition.

types.name: Stabilised NOI
types.explanation: Sustainable income after normalising unusual conditions.

workedCase.setup: Assume stabilised NOI ₹8 lakh and cap rate 8%.
steps: Assess why the rate differs and whether income is sustainable.
workedCase.result: Small rate changes can materially alter value.
workedCase.interpretation: The example assumes income and cap-rate conventions match.

analysis: Stress cap rates and capital requirements.

explanation: Property valuation may use comparable sales, income capitalisation, discounted cash flows or replacement-cost analysis. Each method answers a different part of the question and relies on adjustments for location, condition, leases and rights. A price per square foot alone can conceal major differences.
Use cash-flow projections when lease changes, redevelopment or capex make a single-year income measure inadequate.

types.name: Cost approach
types.explanation: Estimates replacement economics with relevant depreciation.

workedCase.setup: A property generates ₹8 lakh NOI but needs ₹20 refurbishment immediately; a simple income capitalisation gives ₹100 before that spend.
steps: Adjust a cash-flow valuation for the immediate ₹20 outflow.
Avoid comparing the unadjusted ₹100 with a fully refurbished asset.
workedCase.interpretation: The adjustment also depends on future rent benefits and valuation convention.

explanation: Development feasibility compares land, construction, financing and other costs with expected sales or operating value. The schedule matters because spending usually precedes receipts. Planning, contractor execution and demand uncertainty can change both cost and timing.
Profit margin on total cost does not measure annualised equity return. Delays can increase interest and prevent refinancing even when eventual sale value is unchanged.

types.name: Absorption risk
types.explanation: Speed and price of leasing or selling.

workedCase.setup: Expected sales are ₹150 lakh; land ₹40, construction ₹70 and other costs ₹20.
steps: Model delayed receipts and added financing costs separately.
workedCase.result: Thin margins can disappear under plausible execution shocks.
workedCase.interpretation: Tax, permissions and sales assumptions require local verification.

analysis: Test sales pace and financing availability.

explanation: A mortgage is lending secured by property under specified rights. Amortisation divides scheduled payments between interest and principal, with the mix changing as the balance falls. A balloon structure leaves substantial principal for maturity, while floating rates change payments or term under the agreement.
Affordability requires total cash obligations, not only the initial payment. Collateral value does not replace repayment capacity.

workedCase.setup: A ₹100 lakh loan has 10% annual interest and an illustrative ₹15 annual payment.
steps: Closing balance is ₹95 before fees or timing effects.
workedCase.result: Only part of the payment reduces debt.
workedCase.interpretation: Monthly amortisation and rate-reset conventions produce different exact schedules.

explanation: Loan-to-value measures borrowing relative to property value; debt yield compares NOI with debt; debt-service coverage compares defined cash income with required service. They address collateral leverage, income support and payment capacity respectively. Definitions used by lenders can differ.
A higher appraised value can improve LTV without generating any additional repayment cash. Use all three alongside lease and refinancing analysis.

types.name: DSCR
types.explanation: Defined cash available divided by debt service.

workedCase.setup: Property value ₹100 lakh, debt ₹60, NOI ₹9 and annual debt service ₹6.
steps: DSCR is 1.5× under the stated definitions.
workedCase.result: Collateral and cash metrics provide complementary information.
workedCase.interpretation: Capex, reserves and taxes may change the lender's coverage measure.

explanation: Unlevered property returns measure asset performance before financing; levered returns measure equity cash flows after debt effects. Borrowing can raise equity returns when asset performance exceeds financing costs, but also magnifies losses and introduces payment risk.
Compare the same asset, period and cost assumptions. A leveraged return excluding debt repayment or necessary capex is incomplete.

types.name: Equity return
types.explanation: Distributions and sale proceeds relative to equity.

workedCase.setup: A property costs ₹100 lakh and generates ₹10 annual cash before financing; debt is ₹60 at 8%, with no principal repayment assumed.
steps: Equity cash is ₹5.2 on ₹40 equity, or 13%.
A ₹20 value decline halves that equity before other changes.
workedCase.result: Leverage magnifies both income yield and price sensitivity.
workedCase.interpretation: This excludes fees, tax and amortisation.

analysis: Stress income and exit value together.

explanation: Property joint-venture waterfalls allocate cash among investors and sponsors according to return tiers. Capital return, preferred returns and promoted interests can change payout shares at different outcomes. A promote compensates the sponsor beyond its capital percentage under specified conditions.
Model the actual sequence and timing; simple ownership percentages are insufficient. Return-of-capital and return-on-capital rules are distinct.

types.name: Promote
types.explanation: Sponsor's enhanced share above defined thresholds.

workedCase.setup: Assume ₹100 capital, ₹140 proceeds, capital returned first and remaining profit split 80/20 with the sponsor.
workedCase.interpretation: Real hurdles, catch-ups and interim cash flows require a fuller waterfall.

analysis: Check fees, clawbacks and loss sharing.

explanation: Corporate finance funds a company whose lenders look to its broader resources; project finance funds a defined project's cash flows and contracts, often through a separate entity. Limited recourse allocates certain risks but does not mean there is no sponsor obligation.
Project financing relies on contracted revenue, risk allocation, construction completion and a cash waterfall. The legal documents determine who bears each adverse event.

types.name: Project finance
types.explanation: Repayment centred on project cash flows.

types.name: Limited recourse
types.explanation: Sponsor liability constrained by specified terms.

workedCase.setup: A sponsor has two projects; one is financed in a separate vehicle with lender claims limited as agreed.
steps: Model repayment from that project's cash.
Identify completion or support commitments by the sponsor.
workedCase.result: Legal separation and economic independence are different.
workedCase.interpretation: Guarantees can reconnect risks across entities.

analysis: Test project cash without assumed sponsor rescue.

explanation: A special-purpose vehicle holds specified assets and contracts for a project or transaction. It can support clearer ownership and cash-flow allocation, but insolvency remoteness and limited recourse depend on enforceable structure and conduct. Creating a separate company alone is insufficient.
Related-party transactions, guarantees and cash transfers can undermine intended separation or change who bears risk.

types.name: Ring-fencing
types.explanation: Restricts assets and cash to specified uses.

workedCase.setup: An SPV earns ₹15 lakh but owes ₹10 debt service and must retain ₹3 reserves.
steps: Check whether distributions are contractually permitted.
Do not treat all ₹15 as sponsor cash.
workedCase.result: Entity revenue and distributable cash differ.
workedCase.interpretation: Actual protections and restrictions require document review.

explanation: Construction risk concerns completion, cost and performance before operation; operating risk concerns availability, maintenance, input costs and service delivery afterward. Passing a risk to a contractor works only if the contract is enforceable and the contractor can perform.
Completion delay can postpone revenue while interest continues accumulating. Technical capacity and insurance matter alongside contractual penalties.

types.name: Completion risk
types.explanation: Asset not ready on time or budget.

workedCase.setup: A project expects ₹2 lakh monthly operating cash, but completion is delayed six months and adds ₹3 financing cost.
steps: Assess contractor compensation and revised funding needs.
workedCase.result: A delay changes both timing and required capital.
workedCase.interpretation: Deferred revenue is not always permanently lost, so value it by schedule.

explanation: Concessions grant rights to provide infrastructure services under defined conditions; offtake contracts specify purchases of output; public-private partnerships allocate responsibilities between public and private parties. These contracts can support predictable revenue but introduce performance, counterparty and policy risks.
A take-or-pay label does not remove all uncertainty: exceptions, availability requirements and payment enforceability matter.

types.name: PPP
types.explanation: Public/private allocation of delivery and risk.

workedCase.setup: A plant has contracted annual revenue ₹20 lakh if availability exceeds an agreed threshold; operating cost is ₹8.
steps: Base operating cash is ₹12 before other items.
Assess the buyer's payment capacity and renewal terms.
workedCase.result: Contracted revenue depends on conditions and counterparty strength.
workedCase.interpretation: The example assumes no universal concession rules.

analysis: Model termination, expiry and handback obligations.

explanation: Debt sizing estimates borrowing consistent with project cash generation, coverage targets and financing terms. Sculpting shapes repayments to expected cash available rather than using equal principal instalments. It reduces mismatch in the base case but cannot eliminate cash-flow risk.
Use downside coverage, reserves and maturity constraints. Over-optimistic cash forecasts translate directly into excessive debt capacity.

workedCase.setup: Assume CFADS ₹12 lakh in a year and target DSCR 1.5×.
steps: If interest is ₹3, principal capacity is ₹5.
Repeat by year and reconcile final balance.
workedCase.interpretation: Present-value sizing also requires rates, dates and lender definitions.

explanation: DSCR measures cash coverage of debt service in a period. LLCR compares present value of eligible cash during the loan life with debt outstanding; PLCR uses the project-life cash horizon. Longer project cash flows do not necessarily solve a near-term payment shortage.
Specify discount rate, eligible cash and dates. Ratios built from different definitions are not directly comparable.

types.name: LLCR
types.explanation: Loan-life cash PV divided by debt.

types.name: PLCR
types.explanation: Project-life cash PV divided by debt.

workedCase.setup: Debt is ₹50 lakh; loan-life eligible cash PV is ₹65 and project-life PV ₹80; this year's CFADS ₹9 and service ₹10.
workedCase.result: Long-run coverage can coexist with immediate shortfall.
workedCase.interpretation: Reserves and restructuring may address timing but need separate analysis.

analysis: Avoid substituting lifetime value for liquidity.

explanation: Project cash waterfalls prioritise payments such as operating costs, taxes, debt service, reserves and distributions. Reserve accounts protect specified obligations and may be unavailable for other uses. Cash in the vehicle is therefore not all freely distributable to shareholders.
Distribution tests can block payouts even after a profitable year. Track restricted cash separately from available cash.

workedCase.setup: Revenue cash is ₹20 lakh; operations and tax take ₹8, debt service ₹7, required reserve top-up ₹3.
steps: After debt and reserves it is ₹2.
Check distribution tests before paying equity.
workedCase.interpretation: Actual order and reserve requirements follow financing documents.

analysis: Test distribution conditions and reserve adequacy.

explanation: Refinancing replaces or changes existing borrowing and can release equity, lower costs or extend maturity. It can also add leverage, fees and future rollover risk. Equity cash received through new debt is not necessarily operating profit.
Compare the entire future cash schedule with and without refinancing. High early IRR can reflect accelerated distributions while leaving greater residual risk.

workedCase.setup: An asset has ₹40 lakh debt and refinances to ₹60, with ₹2 fees.
steps: Model interest and repayment on the new ₹60 balance.
workedCase.result: The distribution is financed, not newly earned.
workedCase.interpretation: Higher leverage can worsen downside equity outcomes.

explanation: Infrastructure sectors have distinct cash drivers. Energy depends on resource, price and dispatch; transport on traffic and tariffs; utilities on service demand and regulation; social infrastructure on contractual availability and public-service obligations. Sector labels do not imply identical defensiveness.
Map volume, price, costs, capex and contract risk for the actual asset. Public importance does not guarantee investor repayment.

types.name: Energy
types.explanation: Output and pricing or offtake exposure.

workedCase.setup: A transport asset has 1 lakh trips at ₹100 each and ₹6 lakh operating cost.
steps: A 20% traffic decline cuts surplus to ₹2 if costs remain fixed.
workedCase.result: Demand sensitivity depends on operating leverage.
workedCase.interpretation: Debt, taxes, capex and concession terms further affect cash.

analysis: Stress volume, maintenance and contract expiry.

explanation: Property and project finance connects long-lived assets with construction spending, operating contracts, debt schedules and cash waterfalls. Asset economics must be assessed before leverage. Limited recourse shifts specific lender claims to a project structure; it does not remove execution, counterparty or demand risk.

NOI excludes some financing and capital items, while equity cash depends on debt service, reserves and reinvestment. Debt sizing and sculpting match repayment to available cash under covenants. Construction delay can simultaneously postpone receipts, increase interest and exhaust contingency funding.

types.name: Development
types.explanation: Construction costs, timing and completion risk.

types.name: Project finance
types.explanation: Contractual SPV funding with defined recourse and cash priorities.

types.name: Levered equity
types.explanation: Residual distributions after debt, reserves and other required uses.

workedCase.setup: A property produces ₹12 lakh NOI, requires ₹2 maintenance capex and pays ₹6 debt service. Assume no other cash or tax effects.
steps: NOI-based DSCR = ₹12/₹6 = 2×, while a cash measure after maintenance would be ₹10/₹6 = 1.67×.
workedCase.result: The ratio changes with the cash definition; lenders specify their covenant perimeter.
workedCase.interpretation: Do not treat ₹12 NOI as ₹12 distributable equity cash or use a generic coverage formula without the financing terms.

analysis: Forecast asset cash and construction timing.
Read debt, reserves and waterfall definitions.
